one_liner: Binance offers a free, broad REST/WebSocket API with self-serve API keys and HMAC-signed requests, plus a vendor-hosted official MCP server.
auth_notes: Users create an API key in Binance API Management and send it in the X-MBX-APIKEY header. Private requests are signed with HMAC-SHA256 using the API secret. Public market-data endpoints need no key. The fetched pages do not confirm the draft's claim that OAuth (Binance Login) is partner-only, so that claim was removed. The MCP server uses its own scoped authorization flow, which is separate from the REST API.
access_notes: API keys are free for any Binance account, and only trading fees apply. The pricing page that says so is an unverified third-party profile, but a second page agrees. A Spot testnet is listed. Broker, CaaS and Institutional Buy/Sell programs need partner onboarding, but the core APIs do not.
blocker_notes: Each user must create their own API key and secret and sign requests with HMAC. Multi-user use relies on user-supplied keys.

evidence.quote: Log into your [Binance](https://voiceofchain.com/go/binance) account, navigate to API Management, create a new key, and configure permissions.
Free programmatic access to Binance's REST and WebSocket APIs for any authenticated account. Trading is what is billed, not connectivity.
You can grab a binance free api key in under two minutes, and there's no monthly subscription, no credit card required
